catalog_row.title: Heavy-tailed weights at infinite width: the stable process limit
catalog_row.domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
catalog_row.statement: If the weights of a deep fully connected network are iid with an α-stable law (α < 2) and scaled by n^{-1/α}, the infinite-width limit of the network is a stable process rather than a Gaussian process (Favaro, Fortini and Peluchetti). Characterize the training dynamics of such networks in the infinite-width limit: is there an analogue of the neural tangent kernel (a deterministic or random kernel limit), and does gradient descent in this limit perform feature learning?
catalog_row.statement_caveat: The kernel in the stable limit is random (it does not concentrate); training-dynamics results exist for special cases (to verify 2023-25 work).
catalog_row.source: S. Favaro, S. Fortini and S. Peluchetti, Stable behaviour of infinitely wide deep neural networks, arXiv:2003.00394 (2020)
catalog_row.locator: to verify: Favaro et al., conclusion.
catalog_row.why_important: Trained network weights are often heavy-tailed (Martin and Mahoney); the stable limit is the matching probabilistic model.
catalog_row.where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.

status: First-layer freezing unresolved in read dossier and published source; earlier numerical evidence credited. No native closure asserted.
